messages:
anna_dev: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on Mistral-7B after the kernel-router change this morning. 95p generation latency increased ~12% for long-seq (2k+) requests.

kai_runtime: @anna_dev can you paste the profiler output and a representative request trace? is KV-hit-rate unchanged?

anna_dev: attaching a trimmed trace:

```
# profiler run
profiler --model=mistral-7b --seq=2048 --batch=1 --out=/tmp/m7b.prof
# summary
99p_tok_latency_ms: 480 -> 540
kv_cache_hit_pct: 87%
batch_size_dist: mean=2.1, p95=6
```

ravi_ml: interesting — KV hit% looks fine. I retested locally: with FP8-KV disabled latency goes back down to ~495ms p99. suspect kernel selection prefers FP8 path that is slower on this mix.

melissa_sre: noticed increased GC churn on the hosts during the rollout window, could be memory pressure from bigger prefills + eviction churn.

zheng_infra: kernel-router changed heuristics to favor small-head-safe kernels for odd head_dims. For Mistral head_dim=128, that picks an alternate kernel that uses extra workspace for prefetch which hurts long sequences.

kai_runtime: aha — that explains the mem pressure + latency. two levers: revert kernel-router heuristic OR change batching warmup to accumulate longer before choosing kernel.

ravi_ml: I tried a quick experiment: bumping batcher.min_accumulate_ms from 8->25 reduced kernel switches during warmup and 95p latency recovered to +3% (instead of +12%).

anna_dev: numbers?

ravi_ml: 
```
baseline: p95=460ms p99=538ms
router-change+min8: p95=515ms p99=600ms
router-change+min25: p95=474ms p99=555ms
router-change+FP8-kv-disabled: p95=468ms p99=548ms
```

melissa_sre: also saw higher eviction rates when RoPE scaling was applied in the same rollout — prefix warmup increased KVC occupancy, and our eviction policy was LRUnative which thrashes with quantized tails.

zheng_infra: RoPE scale factor 1.03 adds entropy to keys; combined with per-head quantization mismatch we get lower effective dedupe and drops hit-rate by ~4pts on some prompts.

kai_runtime: actionable plan proposal:
- revert kernel-router heuristic for head_dim parity until we have A/B data
- increase batcher.min_accumulate_ms to 20 for canary (reduces kernel thrash)
- add FP8-KV healthcheck that falls back to FP16 if eviction rate spikes
- add a short perf-test in canary that runs long-seq chat traces

anna_dev: +1. also add a tracing flag to capture kernel selection decision in prod for 30m.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated by @kai_runtime: canary-2024-11-03T09:12 -> rolling back kernel-router heuristic.

perf-bot: Canary metrics: p95 latency dropped from 512ms->476ms across canary hosts after rollback. KV hit-rate steady.

anna_dev: thanks. follow-up: ravi, can you file a short postmortem with repro steps and add kernel-router metric? I'll schedule a quick sync to decide whether to keep batcher change or rework kernel selector.

ravi_ml: will do — I'll include repro script and the FP8 vs FP16 KV perf matrix.

zheng_infra: FYI I'll add a safe-fallback circuit for quantized KV that disables FP8 on heavy-prefill workloads.

melissa_sre: tagging infra runbook update for memory monitoring and eviction alarms :memo:

anna_dev: good work team. moving to threads for follow-ups. :rocket:
